definition: The task of converting spoken audio into written text, also known as automatic speech recognition.
details: Speech-to-text systems power applications like voice assistants, transcription services, and captioning, with modern systems built on large neural sequence models trained on extensive labeled audio data.

explainer.lead: Speech-to-text is the task of converting spoken audio into written text, also known as automatic speech recognition. It powers voice assistants, transcription services and captioning, with modern systems built on large neural sequence models trained on extensive labelled audio.

tiers.eli5: It's the technology that turns a recording of someone talking into a written script of what they said.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build these systems as large neural sequence models trained on extensive labelled audio data. Data volume and labelling quality drive the approach, as noted in the term's description.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as converting spoken audio into written text, also known as automatic speech recognition; modern systems are large neural sequence models trained on extensive labelled audio data. No formula or numerical limits are given.

explainer.example: A captioning service feeds a video's audio track to a speech-to-text system, which outputs written captions.
